messages:
maya: Heads-up — quick eval for the Humboldt LoRA merge failed on the numeric-extraction suite. Quick-eval pack: quick-eval-2026-03-19. Regression focused on invoice/order ID extraction.

justin: On it. I can reproduce locally with the int8-merged artifact on our runtime. Failure pattern looks like tokenizer alignment shift: some prompts have an extra token inserted before the numeric slot.

olivia: Ran a small comparison (FP16 vs 4-bit merged). Results: 
```
model_variant | exact_match | f1   | avg_latency
humboldt/base-fp16 | 0.92       | 0.95 | 120ms
humboldt/lora-merged-int8 | 0.78       | 0.84 |  85ms
```

maya: So latency improved but EM dropped a lot. Could be a mismatch introduced during merge + quantization (KV cache offsets or tokenizer id remapping).

justin: Did a tokenizer id dump for one failing prompt:
```
# prompt: "Order #42 — total?"
# FP16 ids: [56, 234, 12, 999]
# int8-merged ids: [56, 234, 6599, 999]
```
The em-dash (or similar punctuation) appears mapped to a different id in the merged artifact.

olivia: Also seeing logits skew on suffix tokens (perplexity up). I'll run a targeted prefix-cache-off smoke to isolate runtime vs merge.

maya: Good. Sam — do you want this blocked from canary? Proposal: run a 5% canary but with automatic rollback if EM < 0.88 or F1 < 0.9 on the quick-eval pack. Also create a focused quick-eval that stresses numeric slots + punctuation variants.

sam: Yes. Open a canary with rollback thresholds EM<0.88 or F1<0.90 :+1:. Tag infra and release-ops. Keep it 5% until we confirm tokenizer fix.

eval-bot: QuickEval report available: https://redwood-internal/evals/2765432100 — summary: regression on 12/50 cases, avg EM delta -0.14. Full CSV attached in the eval page.

justin: I will try a tokenizer.merge_vocab patch to remap the problematic token ids and re-run merge+quant. If that doesn't fix it, fallback plan is to serve the adapter as a sidecar (no weight merge) until we have stable quantized merged artifact.

maya: Pasting the merge command we used earlier — noticed a small typo in the artifact name which might have caused a mismatch:
```
# merge command used by infra pipeline
python tools/merge_lora.py --base humbolt-base --lora humbolt-clientA --out humbolt-merged --merge-method linear
```
Note the typo: 'humbolt' vs 'humboldt'. Will re-run with the corrected repo/artifact names.

olivia: :facepalm: that could definitely explain the mapping mismatch. I'm re-triggering a fresh merge+quant now (using corrected names) and will attach a new quick-eval when done.

sam: Keep updates concise here. Post canary link and quick-eval summary once ready. Thanks everyone.

maya: Will follow up with a minimal quick-eval pack (10 targeted cases) and the canary rollout config in the ticket.

justin: updating the ticket with tokenizer diffs and a short patch diff to try first.

olivia: If the corrected merge still regresses, I'll run a small experiment: quantize after validating tokenizer/prefix id alignment, and then run integer-cast kernels with prefix padding disabled.

maya: Nice. Closing loop later with results.
